prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (2017)

Brexit and sovereignty
- Leave the EU swiftly; repeal the European Communities Act first. Exit the single market and customs union; regain an independent WTO seat and trade policy.
- Six “tests” for exit: legal supremacy (no ECJ/ECHR jurisdiction), full migration control, restoration of a 200‑mile exclusive economic/fisheries zone, full trade independence, no “divorce” payment and recovery of UK assets, and completion by end‑2019.
- Fisheries: leave the Common Fisheries Policy; revoke the 1964 London Convention; end discards; require all fish caught in UK waters to be landed in the UK; create a protection force.

Public finances, tax and cost of living
- Fund priorities from savings: end EU budget payments, cut foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, cancel HS2, reform the Barnett Formula, recover NHS costs from ineligible users.
- No general tax rises; raise the personal allowance to £13,500 and the 40% threshold to £55,000; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000 per person; remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; abolish the TV licence over three years.
- Crack down on corporate tax avoidance; oppose new business burdens; cut business rates for small premises.

NHS and social care
- Additional £11bn annually by 2021/22 for health and social care; integrate services under a single department.
- Lift cap on medical school places; pay tuition for doctors and certain nurses with service commitments; restore nurse bursaries; recruit more GPs and allied staff; scrap hospital parking charges; create professional regulation for managers; end expensive PFI use.
- Tighten eligibility and cost recovery for non‑eligible users; guarantee status of existing EU health workers.

Mental health
- At least £500m extra per year; 28‑day maximum wait; expand school counselling; targeted support for armed forces personnel and veterans.

Education and skills
- Expand grammar, technical and vocational routes; German‑style dual training; abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; languages from Year 1; no primary sex education.
- Abolish tuition fees for STEM and medicine with UK work commitments; restore maintenance grants; strengthen careers and employability education; protect special educational needs choices.

Housing
- Establish a Housing Development Corporation to deliver up to 100,000 factory‑built modular homes annually for first‑time buyers under 40, with resale to the HDC; prioritise brownfield; review housing associations.

Families and childcare
- Broaden eligible childcare providers; wrap‑around school care 8am–6pm; £80m fund to include children with special needs; reforms to family courts; presumption of shared parenting; grandparents’ contact rights.

Elderly and disabled
- Maintain pensioner benefits and triple lock; up to £2bn a year extra for social care; pay travel time and end zero‑hours for home carers; expand dementia research; reform PIP and Work Capability Assessments; increase Carer’s Allowance.

Immigration and integration
- Target balanced net migration to zero over five years via points‑based and work‑permit systems; five‑year moratorium on low‑skilled migration; seasonal visas; five years’ contributions before most benefits/non‑urgent NHS.
- Stronger enforcement against illegal immigration and foreign criminals; status for EU residents present before Article 50.
- One law for all; measures against FGM, forced marriage, “honour” crimes; regulate religious councils; ban face coverings in public places; robust school oversight against extremism.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 20,000 police, 7,000 prison officers; reinstate Stop and Search; keep and expand prison capacity; tackle prison drugs and extremism; deport foreign offenders; revise alcohol licensing; opt out of the European Arrest Warrant.

Defence and foreign policy
- Spend a genuine 2% of GDP on defence plus £1bn extra annually; increase armed forces by 20,000; overhaul procurement.
- Create a Veterans Administration; guaranteed public‑service jobs for qualifying leavers; hostels and housing allocations; limit historic prosecutions.
- Maintain independent nuclear deterrent; support territories’ self‑determination; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship.
- Shift from aid to trade; close the aid department; reduce aid to 0.2% of GNI; focus on disaster relief and measurable outcomes.

Transport
- Scrap HS2; improve existing rail (especially east–west in the North); remove most road tolls; support EV charging; protect diesel owners from new penalties; aid rural buses; review South‑East airport capacity; freeze then reduce Air Passenger Duty.

Environment, food and energy
- New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodlands; brownfield first; curb plastic waste; strengthen marine protections.
- Replace CAP with a UK Single Farm Payment capped per farm; support small, organic, and hill farms; tighten animal welfare (CCTV in abattoirs, export for slaughter ban, clear labelling).
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave the Paris Agreement and EU ETS; diversify energy mix including shale (not in national parks); remove “green” levies and VAT from household energy; lower industrial energy costs.

Democracy and localism
- Replace the House of Lords with an English Parliament; reduce the Commons to 325 elected by proportional representation; restrict postal voting to need; biennial binding referenda via citizen initiatives.
- Local binding referenda on major developments; committee governance in councils; cut waste and keep Council Tax low.
